diagnostic_evidence.quote: A graph is called series-parallel if it can be obtained from a loop or a bridge\footnote{A single-edge graph.} by a sequence of series and parallel extensions, i.e. subdivisions and duplications of edges.
A graph is called 2-connected, if no removal of a single vertex disconnects it.
Loops and bridges are called trivial 2-connected graphs. Thus, 2-sp-graphs are those that can be obtained by series and parallel extensions from a 2-cycle.

issues.failure_explanation: Take two parallel uv edges and a loop at u. Duplicating an initial loop and subdividing one copy produces this graph, and deleting either vertex does not disconnect it. Thus the stated definitions admit it as a nontrivial 2-sp-graph, although it cannot be generated from a loopless 2-cycle. The asserted characterization therefore does not justify the decomposition needed to define W. Moreover, no positive weighting could extend the theorem to this input: for n=3 and k=1 the loop gives a zero coordinate, so the resulting line has least coordinate angle at most arccos(1/√2), strictly below arccos(1/√3).

failure_location.quote: If $G$ is a directed 2-sp-graph on $k + 1$ vertices and $n$ edges, and $B$ is its incidence matrix and $W$ is the diagonal matrix of $G$-induced weights, then the column space of $W^{\frac{1}{2}} B^T$ deviates from all the coordinate $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathds{R}^n$ by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the from-a-2-cycle family the operative definition of nontrivial 2-sp-graphs, explicitly excluding self-loops, and reconcile the earlier definitions and claimed equivalence with that restriction.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's stated graph domain includes inputs outside its weight construction and for which its bound is impossible. The loopless, from-a-2-cycle family and the sharpness examples for every n>k>0 remain available.
issues.title: The stated graph class admits loops outside the theorem's construction
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine but limited restriction of the stated graph class. The source already supplies the restricted family, so all dimension regimes survive without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Distance is the angular target being maximized, whose conjectured upper bound is arccos(1/√n), not 1/√n. For n=2, k=1, the line spanned by (1,1) has d=π/4. With ε=0.001 the displayed test announces a counterexample, although the hypothesis holds in this case because every unit vector in R² has a coordinate of magnitude at least 1/√2. The lower acceptance threshold has the same metric mismatch.

failure_location.quote:
\If{$d > 1 / sqrt(n) + \varepsilon$}
\State \text{Print( "The hypothesis is solved in negative" )} \Comment{(Never seen this)}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1/sqrt(n) by arccos(1/sqrt(n)) in both comparison thresholds, retaining the maximization direction.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm can falsely announce that the hypothesis is disproved and filters candidate subspaces around the wrong target value.
issues.title: The numerical algorithm compares angular distances with a cosine threshold
issues.why_classification: Two local threshold corrections restore the intended angle-based tests without changing the search method or its intended scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$. Based on these empirical results, we will call such subspaces \emph{extremal}.

issues.failure_explanation: This defect persists after correcting the threshold units. Writing α=arccos(1/√n), the acceptance test establishes only α−ε<d≤α+ε, not d=α. For n=2, k=1, the line spanned by (cos θ,sin θ), with θ=π/4−ε/2, passes the corrected test but has least coordinate angle θ<π/4 and is not extremal. The heuristic stopping rule in Optimize does not exclude such an output.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the tolerance band only to nominate candidates. Before insertion into a certified ES, check exactly that max over k-element coordinate sets S of λ_min(P_SS) equals 1/n, where P is the candidate's orthogonal projector. Until such certification is performed, describe the returned list and numerical counts only as near-target candidates.
issues.overall_effect: Returned entries need not be extremal, so the algorithm does not establish its exact output contract or certify the associated numerical counts as counts of exact extremal subspaces.
issues.title: Tolerance-band acceptance does not certify extremal subspaces
issues.why_classification: Preserving the exact postcondition requires a contained spectral-certification step beyond heuristic optimization. Otherwise a limited weakening to approximate candidates is necessary; neither resolution requires new global proof architecture.
